title: Indian-flagged vessel sunk off Al Mukha, Yemen; all 14 crew rescued
brief: UKMTO/JMIC reported a vessel struck by a projectile/uncrewed surface vessel roughly 9nm off Al Mukha in the southern Red Sea, catching fire and sinking; all 14 seafarers were brought safely to Al Mukha port.
detail: No group claimed responsibility, though Houthi forces have repeatedly threatened Red Sea shipping and declared a formal blockade of Saudi-linked vessels on July 20. JMIC's advisory update logged 80 confirmed maritime security incidents in the wider Red Sea/Gulf of Aden/Somali Basin/Arabian Sea theatre since March 1, 2026, with two new incidents since the prior report.

title: PLA naval/air activity around Taiwan ticks up in early August
brief: Taiwan's MND logged 8 PLAN ships and 5 PLA aircraft sorties operating around the island in a single-day snapshot in early August, with 3 of the sorties crossing the Taiwan Strait median line.
detail: The activity follows a first half of 2026 in which large-scale PLA drills around Taiwan were notably absent, but China ran four "joint combat readiness patrols" in May 2026 — an unusually high tempo compared with prior years. Analysts also flag continued development of the Type 076 amphibious assault ship Sichuan, which may operate closer to a light carrier role than existing PLA amphibious vessels.

detail: FDD analysis published Aug 3 argues China's Senkaku incursion tempo — armed China Coast Guard vessels entering Japanese territorial waters and lingering in the contiguous zone — is running at record levels but drawing comparatively little international attention versus Taiwan Strait or South China Sea flashpoints.

title: Low-pressure area over north Bay of Bengal; fishermen told to stay ashore
brief: IMD flagged a low-pressure area forming over coastal West Bengal and the adjoining northwest Bay of Bengal for Aug 7-8, with fishing fleets off West Bengal, Odisha and the north Bay advised not to venture out during the period.
detail: The system is part of the routine post-monsoon cyclonic build-up in the North Indian Ocean basin; it had not been named or classified as a depression at time of reporting, but coastal district authorities issued precautionary fishermen advisories.

title: Indonesia's fisheries ministry reports 92 illegal-fishing vessels seized in 2026
brief: Indonesia's Ministry of Marine Affairs and Fisheries said it has apprehended 92 vessels for illegal fishing so far in 2026, avoiding an estimated Rp360 billion in state losses, as it continues to expand its patrol-vessel fleet.
detail: The ministry says larger illegal-fishing vessels are squeezing out small-scale fishers' catch, underlining the enforcement push. The figures follow a steady cadence of IUU enforcement actions this year against both domestic and foreign-flagged vessels operating in Indonesian waters.

title: Ferry Mutiara Sentosa II catches fire in Java Sea; 17 rescued by passing tanker
brief: The passenger ferry Mutiara Sentosa II caught fire off East Java near Sapudi Island; the Pertamina Patra Niaga tanker MT Transko Arafura diverted and rescued 17 people, working alongside Indonesia's Basarnas SAR agency.
detail: Indonesia's Deputy Transportation Minister confirmed all passengers were accounted for and that SAR operations concluded successfully. The incident is a reminder of the continuing safety gap in Indonesian domestic ferry operations, which has driven repeated fatal incidents in recent years.

title: Mexican Navy seizes over four metric tons of suspected cocaine
brief: The Mexican Navy interdicted a vessel carrying more than four metric tons of suspected cocaine in a Pacific-coast operation, run separately from the US Coast Guard's ongoing Operation Pacific Viper in the Eastern Pacific.
detail: US Coast Guard's Operation Pacific Viper, running since August 2025, passed 225,000 pounds of cocaine seized as of its June 2026 milestone update; roughly 80% of US-bound narcotics interdictions occur at sea, underscoring the scale of Eastern Pacific trafficking that both US and regional navies are contesting.

title: US Treasury sanctions further vessels/entities in Iran-linked shadow shipping network
brief: OFAC added shipping entities and additional tankers to its SDN list this week as part of continued pressure on an Iran-linked illicit shipping network, per a Federal Register notice published Aug 5.
detail: The action follows a late-July designation wave that named tankers including Nireta (Vanuatu-flagged crude tanker), Well Sail (Marshall Islands-flagged chemical/products tanker) and Yehope (Barbados-flagged crude tanker). Treasury describes the broader effort as targeting the network's ship management, flagging and brokering infrastructure rather than only individual vessels.

title: Lloyd's Joint War Committee removes Pakistan from war-risk Listed Areas
brief: The Joint War Committee formally removed Pakistan and its territorial waters from its Hull War, Piracy, Terrorism and Related Perils Listed Areas on Jul 30, ending a decades-long listing and cutting war-risk premiums for Karachi, Port Qasim and Gwadar.
detail: Pakistan's Ministry of Maritime Affairs pursued the delisting through a dedicated committee formed after the issue was first raised with the JWC in March 2026, presenting technical and threat-environment evidence. The change is expected to lower shipping costs and improve competitiveness for Pakistani ports relative to regional peers. Flagged here as a standing regulatory item since it falls just outside this run's strict 7-day window but had not previously appeared in this tracker.

title: IMO signs updated Port State Control data-exchange agreements with Black Sea and Caribbean MoUs
brief: IMO Secretary-General Arsenio Dominguez signed updated data-exchange agreements with the Black Sea MoU and Caribbean MoU on Port State Control at IMO headquarters on Jul 21, expanding cooperation between regional PSC regimes to better track substandard and sanctioned/shadow-fleet shipping.
detail: The agreements feed into the continued development of a global PSC Overarching Database within IMO's Global Integrated Shipping Information System (GISIS), intended to give inspectors worldwide a more harmonized, real-time view of a given vessel's inspection history. The push comes as the dark/shadow fleet — now estimated at roughly 1,300+ vessels accounting for nearly 20% of global oil-tanker capacity — increasingly relies on jurisdiction-hopping and stale registry data to evade scrutiny. Flagged here as a standing regulatory item slightly outside the strict 7-day window given its direct relevance to shadow-fleet tracking discussed elsewhere in this report.

title: China Coast Guard tails Japanese patrol vessel sheltering from Typhoon Dolphin, drawing Taiwan condemnation
brief: During Taiwan's Aug 5-14 Han Kuang defense exercises, China Coast Guard vessel 2304 tailed the Japan Coast Guard cutter Urado as it sailed from off Taichung toward Penghu to shelter from Typhoon Dolphin; Taiwan's Mainland Affairs Council condemned the shadowing as an opportunistic expansion of China's "routine law-enforcement patrol" footprint in Taiwan's EEZ under cover of a weather emergency.
detail: Analysts assess Beijing is using typhoon-driven disruptions as low-cost windows to normalize China Coast Guard presence and law-enforcement-style patrolling closer to Taiwan without triggering a proportionate military response, consistent with the broader grey-zone pattern Han Kuang's 2026 iteration was designed to rehearse defenses against.

title: Grandweld Shipyards to build two offshore support vessels for Bahri Logistics' Ras Tanura operations
brief: Grandweld Shipyards (Dubai Maritime City) signed a newbuild agreement with Saudi shipping major Bahri's logistics arm to design and build two advanced offshore support vessels for operations at Ras Tanura Port, one of the world's largest energy export hubs; delivery is slated for later in 2026.
detail: The OSVs will support offshore functions including vessel-clearance coordination, maintenance assistance, crew transfers, emergency response and inspection support, and will feature upgraded navigation, communication and safety systems. The deal is part of a broader build-out of Gulf offshore support capacity as Saudi energy infrastructure operators seek regionally built tonnage. title: Shipping Corporation of India floats $720m tender for up to six 8,000 TEU LNG-fuelled container ships
brief: SCI launched its largest-ever global shipbuilding tender (issued Jul 31) for up to six 8,000 TEU cellular container vessels — two firm plus four optional — at an estimated $720 million, specifying LNG dual-fuel main engines, ~330m length, 19-knot design speed and 20,000nm range; bids are due Aug 31.
detail: Eligible Indian shipyards get priority via a Right of First Refusal mechanism allowing the lowest Indian bidder to match the lowest foreign offer; yards without prior cellular-containership experience can partner with an experienced foreign builder that has delivered at least two 5,000+ TEU container ships in the past decade. The tender is aimed at rebuilding India's domestic containership tonnage capacity, which has lagged far behind the country's container trade growth.

title: Typhoon Dolphin makes landfall in Zhejiang, China; over 1 million evacuated
brief: Typhoon Dolphin made landfall near Yuhuan City, Zhejiang Province at about 17:30 local time on Aug 9 with winds over 150km/h, triggering more than 1,000 flight cancellations and the evacuation of over 1 million people, including roughly 900,000 from Wenzhou and 390,000 from Taizhou.
detail: Authorities opened more than 1,000 emergency shelters and warned of 250-500mm of rain across central and eastern Zhejiang. Dolphin briefly formed part of a rare three-typhoon simultaneous grouping with Chan-hom and the subsequently formed Peilou, underscoring the unusually active pace of the 2026 western Pacific typhoon season, which forecasters link in part to intensifying El Niño conditions affecting coastal shipping and fishing-fleet operations across East Asia. Kuehne+Nagel estimated more than 2.4 million TEU of containership capacity was stranded after the storm struck, with terminal operations suspended at Shanghai and Ningbo on Aug 7-8.

title: Two SUBCO-linked subsea cables (Indigo West, Indigo Central) fault off Perth in close succession; repairs targeted for Aug 26
brief: The INDIGO West (Perth-Singapore) and INDIGO Central (Perth-Sydney) submarine cable systems suffered shunt faults in quick succession over the weekend of Aug 8-9 inside Australia's federally declared Submarine Cable Protection Zone off Perth; SUBCO's co-CEO Bevan Slattery flagged "very suspicious" vessel activity near the time and location, and the Australian Federal Police confirmed it is assessing a report of crime. As of mid-August the cable consortium's marine maintenance operator was targeting an Aug 26 repair completion, subject to weather and logistics.
detail: Multi-sensor analysis combining AIS, synthetic aperture radar and electro-optical imagery (reported by Windward) identified a UAE-managed product tanker executing a slow "racetrack" pattern directly over the charted cable route during the disruption window, though no cause has been officially attributed and authorities stress this remains unconfirmed. The two cables are among just 16 undersea systems carrying roughly 99% of Australia's international data traffic.

title: Lloyd's JWC redraws Gulf/Red Sea/Indian Ocean listed area (JWLA-033)
brief: Joint War Committee created one large listed area spanning the Persian/Arabian Gulf, Gulf of Oman, Indian Ocean, Gulf of Aden and Southern Red Sea; added Bahrain, Djibouti, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar; removed Pakistan.
detail: The Lloyd's Market Association Joint War Committee's circular JWLA-033 consolidated a large new Hull War, Piracy, Terrorism and Related Perils listed area across the Persian/Arabian Gulf, Gulf of Oman, Indian Ocean, Gulf of Aden and Southern Red Sea, with Bahrain, Djibouti, Kuwait, Oman and Qatar newly added. Pakistan and its territorial waters were removed, reducing associated war-risk premiums and shipping costs for that route. The JWC most recently reaffirmed the listing in a July 2026 review.
